El módulo «Tu app (Git o carpeta)» despl: The «Your app (Git or folder)» module deploys your repository with its docker-compose.yml (the one Docker Creator generates) and updates it every time you apply. If the repository is private: with the https:// address, set a read-only «Access token» (on GitHub, a Fine-grained token with «Contents: Read-only» for that repository; it is stored encrypted in the vault); or use the git@… address and add the «deploy key» shown in «Passwords» to your GitHub/GitLab (read-only). «Read the repository» (in its options, before the variables) fetches the repository on the server, looks at its .env.example and the ${VARIABLE} of the compose file and fills in the options: the app's passwords and keys → «Generate on the server»; the rest → «Variables (.env)» with the example value or empty; keys for other services (Stripe, email…) it tells you to put in «Secret variables» yourself. If your repository has no .env.example (it is normally committed, but not always), «Use a .env from this computer…» reads the .env you use on your computer: passwords and keys go encrypted to the vault («Secret variables») and the rest to «Variables (.env)» with their value; the file is not copied anywhere. Afterwards, check the values meant for your computer (localhost, DEBUG…). More options: «Command after starting» runs on every apply inside the service you name, with the app running (for the database: ./manage.py migrate, php artisan migrate --force…); «Owner of the app folder» (UID:GID, e.g. 1000:1000) if the app does not run as root and gets «Permission denied»; «Maximum build time». While it builds, the run box shows live what it is doing; if it goes 10 minutes without progress (for example, a «development» mode that sits watching files) or exceeds the maximum time, it stops and says which step it got stuck on. Before applying it warns about typical wrong values in «Variables (.env)» (NODE_ENV other than production/development/test, DEBUG=true, *_ENV=development, empty variables). When applying (and also when Simulating) it checks the compose file: variables without a value (stops), ports open to the whole internet and the code folder mounted over the app (warns); if the image does not run as root and mounts app folders, it hands them to its user by itself. The Simulation says whether there are new changes in the repository and which of the app's containers are stopped. «Read the repository» recognises Django (manage.py), Laravel (artisan), Rails, Prisma and Alembic and fills in the command after starting. «Variables (.env)» is edited as rows (name and value, with «Add variable» and «Edit as text»); the ones that need completing or reviewing are highlighted with the reason: empty, example values, misspelt NODE_ENV, DEBUG on, ports open to the internet, development settings, localhost or passwords in plain sight. «Abrir» la ve desde este equipo sin publ: «Open» shows it from this computer without publishing it on the internet.
«Añadir módulos» abre el catálogo en una: «Add modules» opens the catalog in a window, with a search box and by categories. Press one to add it (whatever it needs is added by itself) or, if it is not installed yet, to remove it; it can also be removed with the ✕ on its row. Blue: added; green: installed; with a padlock: it cannot go with another one you already have. Nothing is installed until you press Apply.
«Crear y arrancar» lo deja como un servi: «Create and start» leaves it like a freshly rented server: without Docker or Coolify. «Stop» keeps what is installed; «Delete» leaves it like new.
«Dar de alta» lo añade a Servidores con: «Add» adds it to Servers with its key and fingerprint. Then attach a template to it (for example with Coolify) and press «Apply».
«Exportar…» guarda el módulo en un único: «Export…» saves the module in a single .draupnode-modulo file to give it to someone else (by email, on a USB stick…). It carries its files and the SHA-256 hash of each one. Only modules without problems are exported.
«Hacen falta N MB de RAM» o «N GB libres: «N MB of RAM needed» or «N GB free»
«Importar…» abre un .draupnode-modulo y,: «Import…» opens a .draupnode-modulo and, before copying anything, reviews it: that it is complete (hashes), that it brings no odd paths or links, that it loads fine and what it does on the server (task types, shell commands, Docker images it will download, internet sites) with warnings about sensitive things: downloading and running scripts or installing software, touching SSH keys, sudo or the firewall, deleting from the root, containers with all permissions or with the server's network, files that are not text (they could be programs), invisible characters that hide code, extremely long lines… You can read each file. Importing it runs nothing on this computer; it runs on a server when you apply it, and there as root: it can do anything on that server. The review helps you see what it does, but does not guarantee it is harmless: import it only if you trust whoever gave it to you (the hash says it was not changed on the way, not who made it), and try it first on the test server. If you already have one with that name, you choose to replace it or import it with another; if it is a built-in module's name, always with another name.
«Ir a sus módulos y aplicar» te lleva a: «Go to its modules and apply» takes you to the server page → Modules. Open «Your app (Git or folder)»: «Where the code comes from» = folder (with «Choose…» to change it). In «Variables (.env)», one row per variable: the highlighted ones are those to complete or review, with the reason. Passwords do not go there: «Generate on the server» (NAME, or NAME:fernet / :base64-32 / :hex-32 if the app requires a format) or «Secret variables» (the ones only you have: email, payment keys…). If the image does not prepare the database when it starts, set «Command after starting» (for example, python3 manage.py migrate).

«Simular» dice qué cambiaría sin tocar n: «Simulate» says what would change without touching anything; «Apply» installs it. You can also export a single instalar.sh.
«Simular» no toca nada: dice qué se harí: «Simulate» touches nothing: it says what would be done and warns about what would fail (variables without a value, ports open to the internet…). «Apply» (below, in the fixed bar) uploads the folder to the server (without .git, .env, virtual environments or node_modules, nor what its .dockerignore lists), builds the app showing the progress live, starts it, checks that the containers keep running and that it responds, and stores in your vault the passwords generated on the server. The first time it takes a few minutes.
